title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy IRAS 20351
caption: Galaxy IRAS 20351+2521, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IRAS 20351+2521, 2MASX J20371771+2531377 · constellation Vulpecula · about 450 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: IRAS 20351+2521 has a sprawling structure of gas and dust, scattered with many blue knots of stars. It lies 450 million light-years from Earth in Vulpecula, the Fox, and its image is part of a 2008 collection of interacting and merging galaxies.
Blue knots like these are generally clusters of young, hot stars. NASA classes IRAS 20351+2521 as an interacting galaxy but does not say what it is interacting with.

The wider collection it belongs to was meant to show collisions at many different stages. According to NASA, galaxy mergers were far more frequent long ago, when the universe was smaller and galaxies were crowded closer together. Even violent smash-ups proceed at a glacial pace by human standards, on timescales of several hundred million years, so each Hubble snapshot catches just one moment of a long process.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: The 33-minute exposure gathers far more light than the eye can.

explore: The set of 59 images was released on 24 April 2008 for Hubble's 18th launch anniversary. Most of them were part of GOALS, the Great Observatories All-sky LIRG Survey, which studies luminous and ultra-luminous infrared galaxies with Hubble together with NASA's Spitzer, Chandra and Galaxy Evolution Explorer observatories.
